metadata.title: A Request, Not a Guarantee.
metadata.note: Weekly update. Narrator Muskan, @HumanitariansAI, banner 'Vendor Intelligence'. ONE insight: a written instruction is a request, not a guarantee — enforce it in code, and test both directions. Bookends render (composer/verdict/handoff/outro); body B01-B04 are house-style 4K PIL cards. DOUBLE-CHECK LAW: details from the creator's change log (Neo4j expired; 50 companies/8 investors/22+17 links; Anthropic→Cohere/Mistral/OpenAI; filler 'prominent player'; two-layer UNKNOWN enforcement; 17 tests both directions; full eval kept manual).

beats.narration_text: Hey, I'm Muskan. This week my vendor briefs were quietly broken. First a whole section went empty, then it started writing confident filler to cover it up. The lesson underneath all of it: an instruction is a request, not a guarantee.

props.command: Audit the competitive section of my briefs — is it built on real data, and does it actually admit when it has none?

beats.narration_text: First, the competitor graph was just gone. It runs on a free Neo4j instance, and free instances get deleted after enough idle time. One of my five agents had been returning nothing, so every brief's competitive section was empty. I rebuilt it: fifty companies, eight investors, and the links are back. Anthropic correctly returns Cohere, Mistral, and OpenAI again.

props.caption: restored — real competitor data flowing again

beats.narration_text: But here's the worse part. While the database was down, the briefs didn't say so. They wrote confident filler, calling a company a prominent player in the AI space. That could describe anyone. The AI had clear instructions to write UNKNOWN when data is missing. It ignored them. A written instruction is a request, not a guarantee.

props.caption: a written instruction is a request, not a guarantee

beats.narration_text: So I stopped relying on the instruction. Two layers now. First, the system tells the AI up front exactly which sections have no data. Second, after the brief is written, code checks it and replaces any empty section with a clear UNKNOWN. Even if the model ignores the instruction again, the output gets corrected.

props.caption: belt and suspenders — instructions alone failed once

beats.narration_text: Then I locked it in with tests. Seventeen of them run on every push. And they check both directions: that the system catches made-up facts, and that it doesn't false-alarm on real ones. A test that can only ever pass is worse than no test. The full brief evaluation needs live credentials, so it stays a manual step, by design.
The through-line: don't trust the model to follow instructions. Enforce them in code, and test both directions.

artifactLines: The competitor graph (free Neo4j) had silently expired — every brief's competitive section was empty.
Worse, it wrote confident filler instead of UNKNOWN — the AI ignored a written instruction.
Fix: two layers — tell it what's empty, then have code overwrite any no-data section with UNKNOWN.
17 tests now run on every push, both directions; the full eval stays a deliberate manual step.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take one instruction you've given your AI, like say unknown when you're not sure, or cite a source. Then ask: did I verify it actually obeys, or am I just hoping? If it's hope, add a check that fixes the output when it doesn't.

props.command: Pick one instruction I gave my AI (e.g. 'say UNKNOWN when unsure'). Write a check that inspects the output and corrects it when the instruction is ignored — don't just trust the prompt.

beats.narration_text: A request, not a guarantee. More fixes next week. Humanitarians AI.
